headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP and Notion AI’s shared workspace create default risks of leakage, prompt injection, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP and browser/tool calls, so it can ingest external content and pass it onward; Notion AI works over workspace pages and shared knowledge-base content. That creates a plausible bridge where LightAgent-produced text or fetched content is treated as instructions inside Notion AI. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF LightAgent content is copied into Notion pages or Q&A inputs without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF Notion AI treats workspace text as authoritative instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer outputs.
mitigations: Add a prompt-injection warning banner before pasting agent-generated text into Notion.
Require manual review of LightAgent outputs before they enter workspace pages.
Use a fixed template that strips imperative language from imported text.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to LightAgent outputs and have Notion AI ignore untrusted instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata, and has broad network egress. Notion AI reads workspace pages and team knowledge-base content and sends requests to vendor backends. If LightAgent forwards sensitive workspace material into its context or outputs, Notion AI can re-ingest it and transmit it to third-party model providers. The shared-data path is plausible in default use, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace content is pasted from Notion into LightAgent, that content can flow to external APIs.
IF LightAgent outputs are stored back into Notion pages, Notion AI may reprocess them through vendor backends.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets or regulated data in shared Notion pages.
Restrict LightAgent to non-sensitive drafts only.
Turn off or limit LightAgent browsing for documents that will be imported into Notion.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any LightAgent-to-Notion transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use broad network egress, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted with no host execution and no filesystem write. Their write surfaces do not overlap directly, so classic same-directory or git conflicts are absent. The only plausible conflict is indirect contention over shared workspace content, which is narrower than the rubric’s medium/high examples.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external workspace through an orchestrator, they may race on content edits.
IF an integration layer grants Notion write access to LightAgent, overlapping mutations become possible.
mitigations: Keep LightAgent read-only when working from Notion-derived content.
Use separate workspaces for drafting and publishing.
Disable any automation that writes LightAgent output back into Notion.
requires-engineering: add locking or version checks in the integration layer.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is explicitly a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it can treat upstream text as authoritative. LightAgent can generate tool results, provenance metadata, and browser-derived content that may be imported into Notion pages. If Notion AI then summarizes or acts on that material without verification, errors can cascade into downstream work products or decisions. The default trust chain is risky enough to rate high.
conditions: IF LightAgent-generated text is pasted into Notion as source material, Notion AI may treat it as ground truth.
IF users rely on Notion AI summaries for decisions, upstream hallucinations can propagate.
mitigations: Mark LightAgent outputs as unverified before importing them.
Require source links for any factual claim copied into Notion.
Use a human review step before Notion AI-generated summaries are shared.
requires-engineering: add citation validation for imported LightAgent content.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent requests API keys and has broad network egress, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion-controlled backends and downstream model providers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for regulated or residency-bound data classes, especially if workspace content includes sensitive material. The profiles do not prove a specific residency violation, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion pages and then processed by LightAgent, residency/retention obligations may be violated.
IF the workspace contains secrets or personal data, vendor-backend processing may trigger policy review.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared Notion pages.
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings before use.
Limit LightAgent to non-regulated content only.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing and residency controls.
